body.statement: Pointwise in each reported \(\delta\in\mathcal D\), derive necessary and sufficient observable dual conditions under which replacing the external exposure margin \(q\) by \(q^{\mathrm{case}}\) leaves both sharp endpoints \(L_\delta\) and \(U_\delta\) unchanged. When these conditions fail, the certificate must cover the exhaustive partition: if \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q^{\mathrm{case}},\omega)=\varnothing\), give a finite Farkas certificate of incompatible substituted margins; if that fiber is nonempty and \(\Psi_\omega\) is nonconstant on it, give two compatible full-law lifts with the same \(b\) and \(q^{\mathrm{case}}\) but different ratio values, together with an attaining primal endpoint law and matching dual bound proving a strict mismatch with \(L_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) or \(U_\delta(b,q,\omega)\); if that fiber is nonempty but ratio-constant, including when it is a singleton, give a compatible-law primal witness and matching dual endpoint bound proving that its singleton sharp ratio set differs strictly from \(\Theta_{I,\delta}(b,q,\omega)\).
body.justification: Case strains are selected by infection and can coincide with exposure margins only on a mathematically characterizable invariance frontier.
body.gap: Gilbert et al. (2001) and van der Laan and Gilbert (2023) give sufficient case-only interpretations under exposure restrictions, but not an if-and-only-if sharp-set preservation criterion.
body.consumer: Surveillance analysts learn exactly when readily available breakthrough-strain frequencies can replace costly exposure surveillance and when they cannot.
